hints: Notice the question asks for order of magnitude in $\text{Hz}$, so recall the visible wavelength range of about $400 \text{nm}$ to $700 \text{nm}$.
Connect wavelength to frequency with $c = f\lambda$ for electromagnetic waves, where $c \approx 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate $f = c/\lambda$ using $\lambda \approx 5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ and check which power of ten the result is closest to.
walkthrough: Recall the useful data: visible light has wavelengths of order hundreds of nanometres, about $4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
State the governing relation for all electromagnetic waves: $c = f\lambda$, so $f = c/\lambda$ with $c \approx 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Substitute a typical visible wavelength, for example $\lambda \approx 6 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$: $f \approx (3 \times 10^8)/(6 \times 10^{-7})$.
Evaluate to $f \approx 0.5 \times 10^{15} \text{Hz} = 5 \times 10^{14} \text{Hz}$, so the order of magnitude is $10^{14} \text{Hz}$.

options.A: Too low by about 4 powers of ten. $10^{10} \text{Hz}$ corresponds to microwaves, not visible light.
options.B: Too low by about 2 powers of ten. $10^{12} \text{Hz}$ corresponds to infrared, just below visible frequencies.
options.C: Correct order for visible light. With $\lambda \approx 10^{-7} \text{m}$ and $f = c/\lambda$, $f$ is a few times $10^{14} \text{Hz}$.
options.D: Too high by about 2 powers of ten. $10^{16} \text{Hz}$ corresponds to ultraviolet or X-rays, above visible frequencies.
